name: Ledger
rootCause: Phishing and scams targeting Ledger wallet owners are increasing, and one of the scam websites obtained more than 1,150,000 XRP from victims. This scam uses phishing emails to direct users to a fake Ledger website. On this fake website, the victim was tricked into downloading malware that pretended to be a security update, resulting in the theft of all Ledger wallet balances. According to the fraud identification website xrplorer operated by the community, the XRP obtained from the scam was sent to Bittrex through 5 deposits, but the exchange “cannot freeze XRP in time”.

descriptions.text: Phishing and scams targeting Ledger wallet owners are increasing, and one of the scam websites obtained more than 1,150,000 XRP from victims. This scam uses phishing emails to direct users to a fake Ledger website. On this fake website, the victim was tricked into downloading malware that pretended to be a security update, resulting in the theft of all Ledger wallet balances. According to the fraud identification website xrplorer operated by the community, the XRP obtained from the scam was sent to Bittrex through 5 deposits, but the exchange “cannot freeze XRP in time”.

Ledger users were targeted by phishing campaigns in November 2020 following a prior marketing data breach. At least $271,000 in assets were stolen after victims revealed their wallet recovery phrases to attackers via fake upgrade emails and websites. Ledger's July 2020 marketing data breach enabled large-scale phishing campaigns. Attackers used exposed customer email addresses and personal information to craft convincing phishing emails, leading users to fake Ledger websites and prompting them to reveal their recovery phrases. This gave attackers full access to victims' crypto wallets.
